title: Decision Engine Routing Inspector — internals and explainability logs
content:
Purpose:
Quick design + implementation notes for the Decision Engine's routing/constraint inspector. Focus: how we evaluate constraints and scores, what we log for explainability, and how routing decisions are surfaced for multi-region control-plane policies. This is a working doc — rough ideas, tradeoffs, and action items.

Goals:
- Make per-request decision provenance traceable end-to-end (routing input -> constraint checks -> score components -> final route).
- Keep runtime overhead sub-1ms for constraints common path; allow richer logging behind a sampling flag for deep explainability.
- Support region-aware fallbacks and capacity-tier routing with clear audit trail.
- Provide a compact, queryable explainability log schema for SRE/CS and compliance.

High-level flow (runtime):
1) Request arrives at control-plane gateway with attributes: model, tenant, qos_hint, region_preference, headers (X-org, X-commit), token_cost_estimate.
2) Normalize attributes into DecisionContext (canonical keys).
3) Run constraint filters in a deterministic order (low-cost checks first). If any hard constraint fails -> mark decision as rejected with failure_reason.
4) If soft constraints exist, compute penalty scores per constraint and aggregate into a constraint-penalty vector.
5) Fetch routing candidates (model variants, regions, tiers) from routing-index (cached).
6) Compute base candidate score (latency_est, cost_est, reliability_score) + constraint penalties + policy weights -> final ranking.
7) Choose top candidate; if below threshold, apply fallback chain (alternate region, lower-cost variant, fallback queue).
8) Emit explainability log & traces (sampling controls).

Constraint evaluation order rationale:
- Fast hard rejects first: tenant-suspension, contract-mismatch (dedicated-only request on shared), illegal-region, request-size-limit. These are boolean checks cheap to compute.
- Capacity checks next: region-capacity-snapshot (cached, slightly stale but cheap), tier-availability. These may call in-memory metrics snapshot.
- Soft policy checks last: cost-budget-guardrails, request-rate-anomaly, quality-regression flags (may require eval cache lookup).
Rationale: minimize wasted work; ensure deterministic early rejections to simplify auditing.

Constraint types and hints:
- Hard boolean constraints (reject): contract_clause, compliance_zone, tenant_suspended, model_blacklist.
- Quantitative constraints (thresholds -> boolean): max_seq_len, payload_size, token_budget_remaining.
- Soft constraints (penalties): cost_sensitivity, recent_quality_regressions, traffic_shaping_priority.
- Override channels: admin-bypass-token, rollout-experiment-flag (both audited).

Scoring model (candidate-level):
- base_score = w_latency*(1 / (1 + latency_est_ms)) + w_cost*(1 / (1 + cost_est)) + w_reliability*reliability_score
- penalty_total = sum_i (penalty_weight_i * penalty_value_i)
- final_score = base_score - penalty_total + random_tiebreaker(0-1e-6)
Weights are per-policy and anchored to SLA class (critical/standard/low). We persist the effective weights used in the explainability log for reproducibility.

Explainability log schema (compact, single-line JSON stored in logs/decision-proof):
- request_id: uuid
- timestamp: iso
- tenant_id: string
- model: name@version
- candidates: [candidate_ids] (short list)
- chosen: candidate_id
- scores: [numeric scores aligned to candidates]
- penalties: {candidate_id: [penalty_keys]} (only non-zero)
- hard_rejects: [reasons] (if decision ended in reject)
- constraint_checks: [ordered list of constraint keys evaluated]
- policy_weights: {w_latency: "0.6", w_cost: "0.3", w_reliability: "0.1"} (as strings to keep schema flat)
- routing_path: ["control-plane-cache", "index-v2", "region-us-east-1"] (short trace of subsystems consulted)
- trace_url: optional link to full trace (x-trace id)
- sample_level: enum (none|light|full)
- explain_version: schema version string
Notes: we emit a compact version for high-throughput logging and store expanded traces in the explainability store when sample_level==full.

Example compact log (single-line):
{request_id: r-1234, timestamp: 2025-02-18T14:12:03Z, tenant_id: org-55, model: llama-3b@2025-01-11, candidates: [c1,c2], chosen: c2, scores: [0.24,0.43], penalties: {c1:[cost_penalty]}, hard_rejects: [], constraint_checks: [tenant_suspended, contract_ok, region_ok, capacity_ok], policy_weights: {w_latency: "0.6", w_cost: "0.3", w_reliability: "0.1"}, routing_path: [index-v2,region-us-west-2], trace_url: https://x-trace/r-1234, sample_level: light, explain_version: v1}
Sampling strategy for explain logs:
- Default path: sample 0.05% of successful requests (light) -> compact logs only (no heavy datastore lookups).
- Error path: 100% of requests that hit hard_rejects or fallbacks are logged at light level.
- Anomaly path: if scoring produces unexpected spread (top score - runner-up < epsilon) or candidate scores near threshold -> escalate to full sample for 30s.
- Ad-hoc: engineers can enable full sampling for experiments via rollout flags (audited).

Storage & indexing:
- Compact logs -> high-throughput ELK/Cloud logging (retention 30d). Indexed by request_id, tenant_id, chosen candidate, model.
- Full explain traces -> explain-store (object store + metadata DB) with 90d retention by default. Exposed via Console UI and support debug page.

Performance considerations & optimizations:
- Constraint micro-benchmarks: keep avg constraint evaluation < 300us on p95. Use short-circuiting and local caches for capacity snapshot.
- Routing-index cache: TTL 2s for latency estimates, 30s for capacity snapshots; invalidation via pubsub on model variants/region scaling events.
- Batch checks for bursty traffic: when multiple requests from same tenant arrive in same tick, evaluate tenant-level constraints once and reuse.
- Move heavy checks async: quality-regression detector can be evaluated async and backpropagated into a soft penalty store, not blocking the request.

Multi-region specifics:
- Region preference declared by request -> preferred region considered first. If region capacity shortfall -> candidate fallback to nearest region by configured region_fabric_cost.
- Cross-region cold-start penalty applied to models not warmed in target region. Cold-start signals stored in routing-index and contribute to penalty.
- For compliance zones, hard constraint region_allowed must be true (no fallback to other regions permitted).

Observability & UI integration:
- Console: per-request decision inspector showing compact log and link to full trace, with latency breakdown (constraint evals vs scoring vs routing).
- Alerts: SLO for decision-latency p95. Alert if explain logs sampling rate drops (indicates logging pipeline issue).
- Debug view: replayable decision input + ability to re-run evaluation with modified weights/flags.

Audit & compliance notes:
- All hard_rejects and admin-overrides must be tamper-evident. Signed compact log entries with a control-plane key to detect post-hoc edits.
- Retention policy for explainer logs must satisfy compliance requests (90d by default, extendable per enterprise contract).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
1) How much of the scoring math do we persist verbatim vs pointers to the weights config? Persisting numbers is simpler for repro but increases log size. (tmp stance: persist both weights and final numeric.)
2) How to represent multi-candidate penalty vectors compactly without exploding log size? Consider storing only non-zero penalties and small integer codes.
3) Sampling semantics for high-volume tenants: should we bias full sampling towards larger customers for debugging? (Ops + CS ask yes; privacy concerns from legal).
4) Cryptographic signing of logs: HSM integration required? Need security + infra sync.

Immediate action items:
- [Ethan] spike: implement compact explain log serializer (target 200 bytes avg) and benchmark write throughput (JIRA-PLAT-3561).
- [Maya] prototype sampling controls in rollout service and UI toggles (PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/42).
- [Aisha] draft API for re-runable decision inspector (Confluence draft + minimal REST endpoint for local replay).
- [Ruben] prototype short-lived capacity snapshot cache with pubsub invalidation; measure stale-induced rejects.

Related tickets / refs:
- JIRA-PLAT-3124: Decision Engine rearchitecture (parent epic).
- JIRA-PLAT-3561: Explain log serializer spike.
- github.com/redwood-inference/decision-engine/issues/99: cold-start penalties discussion.

Notes to self:
- Keep log schema stable; bump explain_version when we change field semantics.
- Consider a small SDK for other Redwood services to attach decision provenance (CLI for SRE to query explain-store).

End of notes — rough and iterative. Please add comments inline or update Confluence draft as we converge on schema.
